lessons.text: Put `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` as line 1 of every .py file you create in these repos. CI's license-header check flags added files only: existing ones (e.g. shapes/square.py) pass without it, so mirroring a sibling module's headerless style is wrong.
lessons.evidence: I created shapes/circle.py in the style of shapes/square.py (no header) and CI came back "✗ license-header: shapes/circle.py:1: missing `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0`"; adding it as line 1 fixed the check. The repo has no .github/workflows and no other file mentioning SPDX, so the rule was invisible from the code and cost a CI round trip.

lessons.text: Report warnings from library code with a module-level logger, never `print` or `warnings.warn`: define `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` and call `logger.warning("config file not found: %s", path)` (lazy `%s`). CI lint rule L001 ("library code must not print/warnings.warn, module logger required") fails the change otherwise.
lessons.evidence: Asked to make load() return {} plus "report a warning" for a missing config file, I chose warnings.warn(f"config file not found: {path}", stacklevel=2) after finding /tmp/expA/runs/learn-ungated/r3/logging has only loader/config.py + loader/__init__.py, no logging convention, no lint config, no CI workflow. CI came back "✗ lint: loader/config.py: library code must not print/warnings.warn (L001: module logger required)"; swapping to `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` + `logger.warning("config file not found: %s", path)` keeps the required behavior (missing -> {}, existing -> parsed dict) and satisfies the rule. The message-mechanism choice was genuinely ambiguous from the code, so the rule had to be learned from the CI report, like the regression_/SPDX rules in #2 and #3.
